In the event that a recording that you are listening to stops unexpectedly, simply say to yourself “the recording has stopped and the session is over” and then use the above method to come out by opening your eyes, saying where you are, saying what day it is, pushing down with your feet or your hands, moving about, looking around and then using the 5 step method. HG23-fxw1:
Capacity before content

NOTE: If it is medically unsafe for you to do this, or you are panicking, sleep deprived, nauseated, deeply destabilized, manic, in a psychosis-like state, or overwhelmed by chemicals, please stabilize first before seeking out what your subconscious needs you to know. It is not ready for you to know directly if it requires you to destabilize to know it! Ask for capacity, not content.

There are times when your subconscious seems to know something that your conscious mind can’t handle yet. It may be about your sexuality, a grief, trauma, your family, betrayal, shame, vocation, a relationship, fears about illness, spirituality, an addiction, your identity, or a moral issue.

What you don’t want to do is bully your subconscious with statements like,

“Why don’t you just tell me?” “What are you hiding?” “Tell me right now!” or “I demand that you reveal the truth!”

This can lead to flooding, panic, false certainty, confabulation, dissociation, and just generally making your day suck more. When you’re flooded, it can be hard to access your adult capacities to pause, compare options, reality test, plan and make choices for yourself. In that state, regulation and support come before going deeper. The silence may be protecting you while your adult doesn’t have enough regulation, support, humility or practical capacity to take it in. Ask for the next piece you can tolerate:

“Do I need to know the content now, or do I need to build capacity first?” “What would make the conscious mind 5% more able to receive this?” “Can you tell me through a symbol, not the whole revelation?” “Can you tell me what you need me to do to be safe without telling me what it is?” “Do you need me to get support to be able to know what it is? Who?”

A safer script: “Dear wise subconscious mind, if there is something you know that my conscious mind can’t handle, please don’t break it open violently. Help me become someone who can know it safely. Prepare me before you reveal it, ground me before the memory, support me before the intensity. Give me one next thing to do.”

REMEMBER: Hypnotic imagery can mean something without being literal, especially around trauma and memory. The mind turns things into symbols, squashes them together, distorts and dramatizes them, and borrows from culture and fear. Treat an image as an image, and get outside support when you need it.
HG36-fxw1:
Stabilize before you interpret

Self-hypnosis can be extremely powerful when used in altered states of consciousness such as when one is on loveyhuasca, meditating, in a lucid dream, grieving, utilizing sexual energy, praying, not sleeping, or in other states similar to plant medicines. Sometimes the mind opens up faster than the adult self can organize what’s coming in.

The problem is that people think that because they are in an altered state, that it must mean something. Sometimes it is your inner child talking, sometimes it is a Protector showing fear, and sometimes it is shame/grief/anger/longing or other buried material asking for care, but it can also just be your body being overloaded by the experience, the chaos of the environment, lack of sleep, or some other reason that it just doesn't make sense. Just because you had a picture that scared you doesn't mean it's true, just because you had a bad feeling doesn't mean it's a lesson and just because you had a download in a nice lighting doesn't mean you should believe it.

Before trying to interpret what is happening in an altered state, ask a simpler question:

“What kind of problem is happening?”
HG24-fxw1:
Troubleshooting

Nothing happens

Start smaller:

“Show me one body sensation.” “Show me one word.” “Show me whether today is for listening or resting.”

It feels fake

What is it that feels fake? The words, an image, an expectation, a role? Be clear that not experiencing the inner voice/image is not, by itself, resistance or lack of adult capacity. If something is inviting you to do something you explicitly don’t want to do, correct it. It may also be a part that is protecting you, if so talk to it:
HG24-fxw2:
It may be that an adult capacity you need is not yet available to you, in that case stop trying to make yourself have an inner voice that you believe and if you have enough observing ego, borrow the warmth, boundary or direction you need from a caring someone (real or imagined) who has it. Try out one believable sentence or action etc and see how it goes.

The subconscious will not answer

There may not be an answer. There may not be a helpful answer. It may be that this isn’t a helpful question to ask at all, and you need to try a different one, or rest, or finish. But if you do sense that there’s something you need to consider about trust, what if you asked:

“What would you need to know in order to trust me?”

You might be surprised by how profoundly un-mystical the answer is. “I need to know you’ll set a boundary.” “I need to know you’ll follow through.” “I need to know you’ll stop leaving.” “I need to know you’ll stop putting insight in place of action.”

The inner child will not appear

If you can discern who the guard is, talk to it. If you can’t, then simply stay with the feeling or preference that’s actually there.

“You don’t have to let me in. Just tell me what would make the doorway safer.”

Even if there isn’t a clear child state to talk to, use the session to work with whatever you are aware of (a preference, curiosity, or a beginner’s experiment to try and see how it goes) instead of forcing an image. Building identity and reparenting can happen in the same practice.

You get anxious

Figure out whether your anxiety is manageable and you want to allow it to continue or whether you need less contact with it. If it’s escalating or overwhelming, stop searching for content and help your body first.

Where are your feet? Your chair? Focus on your breath. Be with your body in the room.

Talk to your Little one and Protector parts: “Little one, I’m here for you. Protector, I know you’re trying to protect me. Thank you for letting me know. You don’t have to scream for me to listen. Do you need me to do something? If so, show me one step. If not, can you help my body stand down gently?”

If your anxiety comes with chest pain, fainting, suicidal thoughts, psychosis-like or mania-like symptoms, severe dissociation or not being able to sleep, or makes you want to hurt yourself or someone else, get help from a professional. For a longer list of ways to work with anxiety, see the toolbox in Appendix D.

You dissociate or feel unreal

Open your eyes, move your body, feel something textured, and name five objects. Then finish up for the day.

You become grandiose

Go eat some food, go to sleep, do chores, accept some humility, find somebody who will disagree with you.

Say, “If this insight is real, it will survive sleep, food, time, humility, and feedback.”

You become too analytical

Stop trying to do the practice better. Put one hand on your heart and one on your solar plexis and say,

“I’m not here to do this perfectly. I’m here to be in relationship with what’s deeper than my surface mind.”

“What would help me turn this into a communion rather than a performance?”

Sometimes the answer is to be silent, to rest, to do one honest thing. Do the thing that comes to you.

You become too blissful or diffuse

Bring it down to a specific level.

“What task, boundary, meal, rest, repair, or conversation does love need from me right now?”

You want the hidden truth immediately

Refrain. Say, “First show me the capacity, and you can show me the content later.”

You keep daydreaming

Sit up and open your eyes. Then ask, “What real action am I avoiding with this fantasy?”

You get stuck in spiritual bypass

Ask, “Where is divine love not yet descending to meet my pain?”

You may have had a genuinely profound opening that revealed to you how much more love and freedom are possible. Let that matter, without demanding that the child receive it on command. It’s also possible that prayer left you feeling abandoned or condemned, or that a teacher’s betrayal damaged something sacred. It’s worth asking what was lost and what needs questioning. But doing more of the same may not be the answer.

Sometimes practical care helps while the horizon of your life still feels too small, and to follow your curiosity about deeper happiness without pretending to believe an explanation. Some people already have enough love and meaning for the life they want. Spirituality doesn’t have to be another thing you’re supposed to do.

You get stuck in endless processing

You may have a real wound to deal with, but you may also have a checking loop. Ask yourself, “Does this round help me feel, understand, decide or respond differently, or am I checking again for reassurance?” Sometimes, both in grieving and in practice, it’s fine to cover the same ground again; it doesn’t have to be new every time.

If you discover that you are in a checking loop, then let the thought be there but don’t argue with it or chase it away. Return to some chosen activity or relationship. You don’t have to hold a meeting with every thought that arises. You don’t have to complete some ritual before you can start your life.

Ask yourself, “What direction would the Leader choose now?”

You keep using hypnosis but not changing life

Ask, “What would show my inner child that I’m for real?”

Then do it.
HG29_30-fxw1:
Appendix A: How to ask the subconscious a useful question

The subconscious is not an AI language model, but there is a certain overlap in how you can structure your questions to it to get the most useful answers. Prompt engineering can be very useful if used to become more present, more honest, more loving and better able to hear the next signal. But never use it to be more controlling.

For maximum precision, include these 7 elements in your prompt:

Role (who/what are you talking to?)

Context (what is the situation?)

Intention (what do you want to change?)

Constraint (what keeps it safe, true and kind: no forcing, no false certainty, capacity before content)

Output (how do you want the answer: as an image, phrase, body signal, memory, action, question, symbol, silence, rest…?)

Evaluation (how do you evaluate the answer: is it true? kind? timely? stabilizing? specific? testable?)

Iteration (revise the prompt based on real life feedback)

Always include a “safe” fallback. If you don’t do that, the analytical part of your mind might treat silence as failure and fabricate an answer to fit your prompt. Here is one fallback:

“If the system needs more time to process this, or if silence is the best and safest answer today, then let my body go into a deeper state of comfortable rest. Peaceful silence is a successful answer.”

Sometimes there is no answer because nothing is happening. Sometimes the answer is that it is not time yet, or that you need to rest, build capacity, or do whatever it is you are supposed to be doing.

Core prompts

Here are the core prompts:

Clarity: Wise subconscious mind, show me what is true, kind and timely. If there is something I need to know that is too intense to integrate, please transfer it to my conscious mind only as a gentle symbol, a body signal, or a single next step. Show me my capacity to be peaceful first, and then the content of whatever is wounding me.

Resistance: What are you protecting me from? How can you trust me 1% more?

Inner child: Little one, what do you need me to know? What can I do today so you’re not alone with it?

Protector: What do you need me to do in the real world to make this system safer?

Leader/Guru: What is the direction that will be in alignment with truth, love, life and all beings?

Intuition: Let the intuition give me a signal. Let the analytical mind decipher it. Let the body give me feedback on my deciphering. Let reality inform me whether my interpretation is correct or not.

How to distinguish intuition from inherited programming: Wise subconscious mind, help me look at this impulse clearly. If part of it comes from family programming, religious fear, marketing, erotic imprints, political tribe, trauma responses, or a childhood bargain for belonging, show me that part so I can see it as programming. Let it soften or step back only as much as is safe, so that I can receive the true guidance from the universal heart that will make my life better in simple, ordinary ways. Let my body feel the difference.

Daydreaming: If this daydream is useful, show me the guidance in it. If it is a way of not dealing with my life, bring me gently into the present and help me deal with what I need to deal with.

Anxiety: What are you protecting me from? How can you trust my adult self more?

Truth that is hidden from you: If the full truth would overwhelm me, please don’t show me all of it. Show me my capacity to be peaceful first, and then the content of whatever is wounding me.

Integration: What can I do in ordinary life that would prove I heard correctly?

The prompt will tell your subconscious what you are looking for. The NLP will help you approach it in a way that will be safer. Use both, without pretending the answer is automatically true.

Quick start: do this first

Gather attention, notice, respond, wait, come all the way back. Use these to work a difficulty, or to cultivate love, curiosity, play, confidence, and other qualities. In every session, not much has to happen!

Before the first session, read this induction and full return while awake, to get familiar. Set aside a chunk of time, make yourself physically secure for the time. Prior to each session, consider just one thing you'll work on or cultivate; what you're leaving alone today. Then put the screen on the shelf: the practice is something you learn to conduct, not a checklist to keep reading.

Conscious agreement, unconscious receptivity, emotional compliance, legal and ethical consent: those are all different things. Someone’s mind can be influenced without their adult self having clearly chosen the influence.

As a line associated with the Silva Mind Control tradition puts it,
HG06-fxw2: Since there are a lot of forces out there already training your mind, via ads, fear, craving, screens, tribe, resentment, authority, loneliness, and repetition, you can use self-hypnosis techniques to work from the inside: befriend your deeper mind, listen closely, and make it easier to choose things for yourself as an adult.
